subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 geography question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with an example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Continents and oceans of the world
Hemispheres, the Equator and the Prime Meridian
The geographical regions of the UK

questions.lo: Continents and oceans of the world
questions.q: How many continents and how many oceans is the world usually divided into?
questions.explain: The world is usually divided into 7 continents (Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia/Oceania, Europe, North America, South America) and 5 oceans (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic).

questions.lo: Continents and oceans of the world
questions.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering roughly a third of the Earth's surface. The Atlantic is the second largest.

questions.q: A student writes: 'Africa is a country in Asia.' What is wrong with this statement?
options: Africa is a continent, not a country, and it is not in Asia
Nothing is wrong, it is correct
Africa is a country but it is in Europe
Africa is an ocean, not a country
questions.explain: Africa is a continent (a huge landmass made up of over 50 countries), not a single country, and it is its own continent, separate from Asia.

questions.q: Which country is the largest in the world by land area and spans both Europe and Asia?
questions.explain: Russia is the largest country by area and stretches across both Europe and Asia. Canada is second largest but lies only in North America.

questions.q: Which two countries, both in Asia, have the largest populations in the world?
questions.explain: China and India, both in the continent of Asia, are the two most populous countries on Earth.

questions.q: The Middle East is a significant world region best described as which of the following?
options: A single country in South America
A region where Asia, Africa and Europe meet, and a major source of oil
A continent made only of desert
A group of islands in the Pacific Ocean
questions.explain: The Middle East lies where Asia, Africa and Europe meet, and it is one of the world's major sources of oil.

questions.q: Which of these is a physical (natural) feature rather than a human feature?
questions.explain: Mountains are natural, so they are a physical feature. Cities, motorways and borders are all built or created by people, so they are human features.

questions.q: Which statement correctly sorts these features?
options: A river is human; a bridge is physical
A river is physical; a bridge is human
questions.explain: A river is natural, so it is a physical feature. A bridge is built by people, so it is a human feature. The test: would it exist without people?

questions.q: A biome is best described as which of the following?
options: A large region defined by its climate, plants and animals
A line drawn on a map by people
questions.explain: A biome is a large region with a shared climate and characteristic plants and animals, such as tropical rainforest, desert or tundra. Biomes follow climate, not country borders.

questions.q: Lines of latitude run in which direction?
questions.explain: Lines of latitude run horizontally, parallel to the Equator, telling you how far north or south you are. (Lines of longitude are the vertical ones.)

questions.q: A common mistake is to mix up the two zero lines. Which pairing is correct?
options: Both the Equator and Prime Meridian are 0° latitude
Both the Equator and Prime Meridian are 0° longitude
questions.explain: The Equator is 0° latitude (halfway between the poles), and the Prime Meridian is 0° longitude (through Greenwich). Keeping these two zeros separate is a key skill.

questions.lo: Hemispheres, the Equator and the Prime Meridian
questions.q: Which line divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern hemispheres?
questions.explain: The Equator (0° latitude) splits the Earth into the Northern and Southern hemispheres. The Prime Meridian splits it into the Eastern and Western hemispheres.

questions.lo: Hemispheres, the Equator and the Prime Meridian
questions.q: The Prime (Greenwich) Meridian is at 0° longitude and passes through which city?
questions.explain: The Prime Meridian is 0° longitude and runs through Greenwich in London, which is why it is also called the Greenwich Meridian.

questions.q: Which pair of lines of latitude lie either side of the Equator and mark the edges of the tropics?
options: The Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn
The Prime Meridian and the Equator
The North Pole and the South Pole
questions.explain: The Tropic of Cancer (north of the Equator) and the Tropic of Capricorn (south of the Equator) mark the edges of the tropics, where the Sun can be directly overhead.

questions.q: The Arctic Circle and the Antarctic Circle surround which parts of the Earth?
options: The hot deserts near the Equator
The very cold far north and far south
questions.explain: The Arctic Circle surrounds the cold far north, and the Antarctic Circle surrounds the cold far south — the regions around the North and South Poles.

questions.q: World time zones are measured east and west from which line?
questions.explain: Time zones are measured east and west from the Prime Meridian at Greenwich (GMT). They follow lines of longitude, not latitude.

questions.q: It is midday in London. Compared with London, what is most likely true about the time in China, which lies to the east?
options: It is exactly the same time
China does not use time zones
questions.explain: Travelling east, clocks are ahead, so it is later in China than in London — it would already be evening there when it is midday in London.

questions.lo: The geographical regions of the UK
questions.q: Which four countries make up the United Kingdom?
options: England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland
England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
questions.explain: The UK is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. The Republic of Ireland is a separate, independent country.

questions.lo: The geographical regions of the UK
questions.q: What is the difference between 'Great Britain' and the 'United Kingdom'?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Great Britain is the island of England, Scotland and Wales; the UK also includes Northern Ireland
Great Britain includes Ireland; the UK does not
The UK is only England; Great Britain is everything else
questions.explain: Great Britain is the island containing England, Scotland and Wales. The United Kingdom adds Northern Ireland, so the two terms are not the same.

questions.lo: The geographical regions of the UK
questions.q: Which of these is an example of key UK topography (physical landscape)?
questions.explain: The Scottish Highlands are a major upland (mountainous) region — an example of the UK's physical topography. Cities, motorways and counties are human or administrative, not physical relief.
